mission: The full scope reveals: the Ruusan Reformations as penance, the forbidden technique, the wound at Veranthos, the anchor system, the Brotherhood's lattice inversion attempt
why_now: Sera and Torin recognize the archive and can interpret what Ben couldn't — the conceptual vocabulary returns with its original speakers
conflict: The information is staggering in scope — Ben's understanding of Jedi history is being rewritten in real time. Sera and Torin disagree on emphasis; Kael corrects details from the Sith perspective that neither expected.
turning_point: The Reformations — the foundation of modern Jedi identity, the thing Ben grew up being told was principled reform — were penance. Damage control. The Order has been built on institutional amnesia.
opening_hook: Sera's voice fills the archive level like she belongs there. She does. She was the one who organized half of it.
closing_hook: The technique. The wound. The seal. The anchors. Twelve Force-sensitives used as structural rebar in a containment system. Nine dead. Three just woken. One escaped.
emotional_trajectory: Absorbing shock -> intellectual vertigo -> moral reckoning with institutional history

stakes.personal: Ben's identity as a Jedi is built on the Reformations' narrative — that narrative is a lie
stakes.interpersonal: The survivors' conflicting accounts reveal they weren't all willing participants
stakes.external: The wound exists, the seal is failing, and the Order doesn't know any of this

setting: Fortress Level 2 (Archive) — survivors navigating familiar territory with thousand-year-old muscle memory
sensory_details: Archive media activating under Sera's touch; holographic displays showing maps of the wound's expansion over centuries; Torin's hand brushing a console with familiarity that makes Ben's skin crawl; the Codex fragment glowing faintly in its sealed case
promises_planted: The institutional lie must be told to the Order (PP08)
The Jacen parallel will be recognized (PP07)
notes: R04 is the major First Plot Point revelation. Dense information delivery but through character perspective, not lecture — Sera's precision, Torin's narrative warmth, Kael's dry corrections. Jacen mentioned during galactic history briefing — Ben's tone tells the reader everything.
